paragraphs.context: If it had not been for Laurie, and old Esther, the maid
paragraphs.mainIdea: Amy finds life at Aunt March's hard. The parrot and the dog are bad, and only Laurie and Esther make it bearable.
paragraphs.simple: Without Laurie and old Esther, the maid, Amy felt she could never have got through that terrible time. The parrot alone was enough to drive her mad. He soon felt that she did not admire him, and he took revenge by being as naughty as he could. He pulled her hair whenever she came near him. He upset his bread and milk to annoy her just after she had cleaned his cage. He made Mop bark by pecking at him while Madam slept. He called her names in front of visitors, and in every way acted like a bad old bird. She could not stand the dog either. He was a fat, cross animal who snarled and barked at her when she washed and brushed him. When he wanted food, which was about twelve times a day, he lay on his back with his legs in the air and a very silly look on his face. The cook was bad-tempered, the old coachman was deaf, and Esther was the only one who ever paid any attention to the young lady.

sentences.context: So she took Amy in hand, and taught her as she herself had been taught sixty years ago
sentences.simple: So she took charge of Amy and taught her in the way she herself had been taught sixty years before.
sentences.grammar: 'Take in hand' is a phrase meaning 'take charge of'. 'As she herself had been taught' is a past passive clause that compares how she taught Amy with how she had been taught.

take in hand.meaning: To take charge of someone and teach or control him.
take in hand.example: So she took Amy in hand, and taught her
